accuracy.evidence: Checked against the PSHE Association Programme of Study KS2 (recognise and manage dilemmas, values and beliefs can conflict, when it is right to break a confidence or share a secret: a secret that puts someone at risk goes to a trusted adult) and CASEL's responsible decision-making competence (consequences for self and others, ethical standards and safety). The lesson never claims one right answer to every dilemma; the adult text notes that fair people can disagree on close cases, and only the safety case is treated as clear.

misconceptions.evidence: Each documented slip gets its own feedback: one side must be bad (values prediction, Why are dilemmas hard challenge), a promise outranks danger (weigh prediction, Ben's secret, hurt-at-home challenge), counting reasons not their seriousness (weights 4/2/2/1/1 so Keep has three cards yet loses 6 to 4), popularity or not getting caught as reasons (reason sort, bullying challenge), and only two extreme options (third-way step: horrible vs pretend, quiet vs tell the class).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagdilem is built around a drawn balance beam: the two named values sit on its pans, then five weighted consequence cards dragged to Tell or Keep visibly tip the beam (Tell 6 : Keep 4), followed by a two-box reason sort that lists placed cards inside each box and a third-way picker per case. This is different from flagright's face and trust-hearts lab for 5-7s (Right and Wrong Choices); gate_lab_distinct passes on 6-token shingles.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner predicts first, then acts with immediate consequences: picking the wrong pair clears the scale and names the real tension (Keeping your promise is Loyalty, Ben being in danger is Safety); each card placed on the wrong side explains which side it argues for; the beam tilts after each card so the learner sees three Keep cards lose to one serious harm. Show me completes every task on iPhone 13 and desktop.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions target the step's idea: In a really hard choice one side is bad vs both sides care about something good; a secret that could get him badly hurt: keep it vs tell a trusted adult; when two values clash the best choice gives one up vs often respects both. The wrong option in each is the misconception listed in the adult paragraph, and the done message reports the learner's own prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six fresh challenge items (found £10, bullying reason, hurt-at-home secret, loyal and fair in a game, which harm weighs most, why dilemmas are hard) with answers rotated each round. Every wrong answer has a specific coach() message, for example Tell other kids gets Other kids cannot keep him safe. A trusted adult can., and Let the friend cheat gets loyal but unfair to everyone else.

readability.evidence: Learner audience: kid explanation FK about 3.0 (limit 7.0) and adult FK 5.8 (limit 10.0). Terms are named and defined in context: dilemma, values, consequences, trusted adult, third way. Canvas prompts are one sentence (Which two values pull against each other? Tap or drag two onto the scale.) and cards are short, everyday scenarios for 9-11s.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph carries a step of the routine with a concrete case: Gran's jumper for Honesty vs Kindness, Ben at the lake after dark for Loyalty vs Safety, the team captain for Loyalty vs Fairness, and named non-reasons. gate_content passes the filler and similarity checks, and the family tip is a specific dinner-table routine.

mobile.evidence: Walked on iPhone 13 and desktop 1200x900 in dark and light. After resizing, the beam span is capped at (width-28)/1.4 so both pans stay inside the canvas; the reason boxes measure each wrapped line so long cards do not overlap; option strips fit three per case. Every drag has a button twin (value chips, Reason to Tell / Keep, Good / Not a real reason, choice buttons). No console errors.

accessibility.evidence: axe wcag2a, wcag2aa and wcag21aa clean in both themes in the browser gate. The canvas aria-label is updated by announce() with every result (Ben trusted you with a secret goes on Keep, weight 2), all actions are real buttons with aria-labels such as Put Honesty on the scale, the challenge feedback is an aria-live status, and the subline under each case uses the main text colour rather than amber for contrast in the light theme.

sources: PSHE Association (2020) Programme of Study for PSHE Education, Key Stage 2: Relationships (recognise and manage dilemmas; keeping something confidential or secret, when to break a confidence; secrets and surprises) and Living in the Wider World (values and beliefs)
CASEL (2020) SEL Framework: responsible decision-making (evaluating consequences for personal, social and collective well-being)
Department for Education (2019) Relationships Education statutory guidance: being safe, when to share a secret with a trusted adult
